schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT T1.PRODUCT_ID,T2.PRODUCT_NAME FROM SALES T1 JOIN PRODUCT T2 ON T1.PRODUCT_ID=T2.PRODUCT_ID WHERE SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' AND T1.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN ( SELECT DISTINCT T1.PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES T1 JOIN PRODUCT T2 ON T1.PRODUCT_ID=T2.PRODUCT_ID WHERE SALE_DATE < '2019-01-01' OR SALE_DATE > '2019-03-31' )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.PRODUCT_ID,T2.PRODUCT_NAME FROM SALES T1 JOIN PRODUCT T2 ON T1.PRODUCT_ID=T2.PRODUCT_ID WHERE SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' AND T1.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN ( SELECT DISTINCT T1.PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES T1 JOIN PRODUCT T2 ON T1.PRODUCT_ID=T2.PRODUCT_ID WHERE SALE_DATE < '2019-01-01' OR SALE_DATE > '2019-03-31' )
explanation: Q1 selects products whose all sales occurred strictly between 2019-01-01 and 2019-03-31 (inclusive of both dates). Q2 selects products that have at least one sale in the range 2019-01-01 to 2019-03-31 and no sales outside this range. This leads to different results when a product has sales both inside and outside the range.
counterexample_dsp: A product with one sale on 2019-01-01 and one sale on 2018-12-31 will be excluded by Q1 but included by Q2.
